headline: PM inaugurates July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum in Dhaka; opens to public Thursday
summary: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman officially opened the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum today, preserving the history of a significant national event. It will welcome general visitors from Thursday.
details: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman officially inaugurated the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum on Wednesday, August 5, at 9 AM. He unveiled the plaque as the chief guest at the ceremony.

Following the inauguration, the Prime Minister toured the museum's various galleries, inspecting preserved artifacts, photographs, documents, and memorabilia. He was accompanied by former Chief Adviser of the interim government, Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, along with other advisors and cabinet members.
On the opening day, the museum was reserved exclusively for special guests and members of the July Martyrs' families. It will open its doors to the general public starting Thursday, August 6.
Visitors will be able to purchase tickets online for entry. The ticket price has been set at BDT 50 for adult visitors and BDT 25 for children.
caption:
Bangladesh's history is now more accessible! The July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum has been officially inaugurated by Prime Minister Tareque Rahman.

Prime Minister Tareque Rahman officially inaugurated the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum on Wednesday, August 5, at 9 AM. He unveiled the plaque as the chief guest at the ceremony.

Following the inauguration, the Prime Minister toured the museum's various galleries, inspecting preserved artifacts, photographs, documents, and memorabilia. He was accompanied by former Chief Adviser of the interim government, Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, along with other advisors and cabinet members.

On the opening day, the museum was reserved exclusively for special guests and members of the July Martyrs' families. It will open its doors to the general public starting Thursday, August 6.

Visitors will be able to purchase tickets online for entry. The ticket price has been set at BDT 50 for adult visitors and BDT 25 for children.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline: 52 tons of green chillis imported from India in two days
summary: Bangladesh brings in a massive shipment of green chillis from India to manage local supply and prices.
details: Bangladesh has imported 52 tons of green chillis from India over the course of just two days.
The import move is aimed at stabilizing the market and ensuring a steady supply of the essential vegetable for consumers.
Green chillis are a staple in Bangladeshi cuisine, and price fluctuations often impact daily household budgets.
The government typically allows imports from India when local production falls short or prices spike in the domestic market.
caption:
52 tons in just 48 hours. Bangladesh ramps up green chilli imports from India to stabilize the market.

Bangladesh has imported 52 tons of green chillis from India over the course of just two days.

The import move is aimed at stabilizing the market and ensuring a steady supply of the essential vegetable for consumers.

Green chillis are a staple in Bangladeshi cuisine, and price fluctuations often impact daily household budgets.

The government typically allows imports from India when local production falls short or prices spike in the domestic market.
